summary: Gives three ways for a collection in Ansible to get into the release changelog: antsibull-changelog, a hand-written changelog.yaml, or an issue on ansible-build-data linking to its own notes. The first two require the changelog to be in the Galaxy release.
questions: Do I have to use antsibull-changelog to be included in the Ansible changelog?
Can I just link my own release notes into the Ansible changelog?
Where does Ansible get my collection's changelog from?

answer_card.title: Include a collection changelog in Ansible
answer_card.answer_md:
Options:
1. Use `antsibull-changelog`.
2. Ship a correctly formatted `changelog.yaml` in your collection.
3. Open an issue at `ansible-community/ansible-build-data` with a link to your own changelog or release notes.

For options 1 and 2, Ansible pulls from **Galaxy**, so the changelog must be in the collection version published there for that release.
